words.prose: {{ar:مَّرْفُوعَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:marfūʿatin}}) opens 80:14 in mid-description: its feminine singular genitive agreement carries the pages from 80:13 across the ayah boundary, so the pages remain the unspoken head. The singular feminine concord also gathers the plural pages as one written medium; elevation lands on the archive-like whole, not leaf by leaf. The passive participle makes elevation a received condition on the pages, not an event of lifting and not self-ascent. The root pressure narrows to conferred height as rank and guarded reach: the written medium is lifted above ordinary handling and ordinary valuation, while unrelated root branches stay outside the local sense. Because this adjective comes before the next adjective, the sequence establishes hierarchy first, then lets purity specify the integrity of that elevated access. Its recited mīm onset also welds the word to the prior adjective in 80:13, and its raised-object field can be heard beside raised houses and objects (24:36; 88:13; 56:34; 52:5) while the local referent remains the written pages prepared before the hands of 80:15 appear.

topics.headline: cross-ayah adjective chain
topics.summary: The adjective depends on the pages named in 80:13 and keeps the nominal description open across the ayah boundary.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 80:14 does not begin a new sentence; it requires the pages of 80:13 to be carried forward as the head of the description.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a feminine singular indefinite genitive passive participle continuing the prior adjective chain, so the CRITICAL claim about cross-ayah dependency is locally licensed.

topics.headline: collective medium concord
topics.summary: Singular feminine concord gathers the plural pages into one qualified written medium.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees elevation assigned to the written medium as a whole, not scattered leaf by leaf across separately counted sheets.
topics.reason: The local grammar marks singular feminine agreement for a non-rational plural head, preserving the collective-medium payoff without making it a separate subject.

topics.headline: conferred raised status
topics.summary: The passive participle foregrounds the achieved raised condition while leaving the raiser outside the line.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pages do not rise or present their own superiority; their elevated rank is received and already settled.
topics.reason: The passive participial form supports received status and blocks reflexive self-elevation or a finite narrated raising event.

topics.headline: height as rank and guarded reach
topics.summary: The broad root image survives as vertical rank and access separation, while other dictionary branches do not govern this local participle.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that elevation is more than storage height: it makes the pages ranked above ordinary valuation and guarded from ordinary reach.
topics.reason: V4 lists many accepted root branches, but the written-page referent and passive participial adjective license the elevation/rank branch rather than specialized branches such as announcing, crop handling, gait, or grammar case.

topics.headline: rank before purity
topics.summary: The first adjective in the two-word ayah establishes elevation before the next adjective specifies purified integrity.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the order: the medium is first ranked high, then its access is qualified by purity rather than by distance alone.
topics.reason: The local adjacency of the two passive participles and their order support a paired status logic without collapsing the two roots into one meaning.

topics.headline: raised-object echoes
topics.summary: Other raised-object scenes provide a useful echo, but they do not replace the local written-page referent.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the pages join a Quranic field of raised, protected objects and places (24:36; 88:13; 56:34; 52:5) while still reading this ayah as a page-description.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah echoes are concrete and coherent, but they are narrowed to resonance and contrast because the local grammar attaches the adjective to the pages from 80:13.

topics.headline: recited boundary fusion
topics.summary: The strengthened mīm onset audibly carries the prior adjective into this one.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the honored pages of 80:13 flow into raised pages in 80:14 before the grammar is analytically unpacked.
topics.reason: The row family concerns audible surface continuity; it is compatible with the attachment evidence that treats the descriptors as one continuing adjective chain.

topics.headline: rank before handling
topics.summary: The raised status is set before 80:15 introduces hands and bearers.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that later handling in 80:15 meets an already elevated medium, rather than creating its rank.
topics.reason: The forward bridge is a discourse payoff from the preserved sequence; no guardrail evidence blocks reading 80:15 as subsequent handling.

words.gloss_range: purified, made clean, cleared from defilement or corrupting mixture; here narrowed to completed purified fitness for the written medium
words.root_gloss_range: broad root range includes material cleanness, ritual purity, purity after menstruation, purifying water, moral cleansing, sacred-place purification, and cleaner lawful choice; the local passive participle selects effected purification as protected textual integrity and fitness for contact
words.prose: {{ar:مُّطَهَّرَةٍۭ}} ({{tr:muṭahharatin}}) completes the same cross-ayah adjective chain: it remains feminine singular, indefinite, and genitive, so purity belongs to the same pages carried from 80:13 as one written medium, not as separately purified leaves. Its Form II passive participle makes the pages objects already purified, not self-purifying and not merely described as naturally clean. The broad {{ar:ط ه ر}} ({{tr:ṭ-h-r}}) field narrows here to cleared fitness for contact and transmission: material cleanness, ritual worthiness, moral freedom from blemish, and freedom from corrupting mixture converge as integrity for the written medium. After the first adjective, this final adjective keeps height from becoming distance only; the elevated pages are also purified for guarded access. Its strengthened mīm onset and repeated -atin cadence make the movement from elevation into purification audible as one connected adjective pair while the two roots stay distinct. Echoes with purified contact and sacred preparation (22:26; 56:79; 98:2; 4:57; 3:15; 2:25) remain useful, but the local landing point is the pages themselves, purified before 80:15 names the hands that bear them.

topics.headline: second adjective chain
topics.summary: The second adjective repeats the agreement pattern and confirms that the whole ayah depends on the pages from 80:13.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that purity is not a new subject or detached predicate; it is the next quality of the same carried-over pages.
topics.reason: The QAC-compatible grammar and attachment notes describe a coordinated adjective following the first passive participle in the same feminine singular genitive sequence.

topics.headline: effected purified state
topics.summary: Form II passive morphology presents purification as completed upon the pages rather than as their own action or a process noun.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pages as already rendered fit by purification, not as naturally clean objects or as agents seeking purity.
topics.reason: The passive participial form and the Form II value support completed effected purification while excluding self-purification, mere evaluation, or a foregrounded purification process.

topics.headline: purity as transmission fitness
topics.summary: The broad purity field survives as cleared fitness for contact, worthiness, and medium integrity, while unrelated applications of the root are not locally selected.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that purity protects the medium's authority from corrupting access and mixture; it is not decorative praise of clean surfaces.
topics.reason: V4 confirms multiple accepted root branches, but attachment to written pages narrows the payoff to purified fitness for protected transmission and contact rather than menstrual, water-medium, or legal-comparative branches.

topics.headline: rank completed by integrity
topics.summary: The second adjective answers the first by adding purified integrity to elevated rank.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that raised status is not left as remote height; purity turns elevation into guarded, trustworthy access.
topics.reason: The local order and close apposition support a two-step status logic: elevation first, then purified integrity.

topics.headline: purity as closure
topics.summary: The ayah lands on purified fitness rather than ending with height alone.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the final emphasis of the two-word ayah fall on cleansed fitness as the last quality before the next ayah names bearers.
topics.reason: The surface order places this adjective last in 80:14, giving the closure claim a concrete local basis.

topics.headline: sacred-contact echoes
topics.summary: Purified-contact and sacred-place parallels illuminate fitness for approach, but they remain echoes rather than the governing local parse.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect purified pages with sacred preparation and qualified contact (22:26; 56:79; 98:2; 4:57; 3:15; 2:25) while keeping the local focus on the written medium.
topics.reason: The cited parallels are concrete and compatible with the passive-participle field, but the local adjective still modifies the pages from 80:13.

topics.headline: paired sound and cadence
topics.summary: The mīm onset and repeated -atin cadence bind the two adjectives as a single heard unit.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears elevation carry into purification in one connected adjective chain, even while the two roots keep distinct meanings.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows describe surface continuity that matches the grammatical evidence for paired adjectives in one sequence.

topics.headline: purity before handling
topics.summary: The pages are purified before 80:15 introduces the hands that bear them.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the next ayah's handling encounters a medium already cleared for transmission, rather than supplying that fitness afterward.
topics.reason: The forward bridge is licensed by sequence: this word closes 80:14 before 80:15 names hands and bearers.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Elevation and cleansing secure the reminder from the opening misvaluation.** `مَّرْفُوعَةٍ` activates raising upward (`ر ف ع` B001) and high rank (`ر ف ع` B002); `مُّطَهَّرَةٍ` activates purity with defilement removed (`ط ه ر` B001). I infer that the paired passives assign the sheets a value and integrity not conferred by socially prestigious recipients. The ayah reads as an objective re-ranking of the message.
2. **A later water-and-harvest mechanism enters the description.** `ط ه ر` includes a purifying water or medium (`ط ه ر` B004), while `ر ف ع` includes bringing in the crop (`ر ف ع` B006). The later poured water and produced food activate these branches as a material sequence: cleansing medium enables growth and raised harvest. That causal transfer is mine. The sheets can thus read as purified yield, analogous to provision, while remaining grammatically the fixed objects described.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:25-32 unexpectedly joined purifying medium (`ط ه ر` B004) to harvested yield (`ر ف ع` B006). The sheets' elevation and purity consequently acquired a material analogy to provision produced through water and growth.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Physical elevation and high rank reinforce rather than replace one another.** `ر ف ع B001` supplies raising upward and `ر ف ع B002` supplies elevated rank. The adjectives modify written sheets at 80:13, while `مُّكَرَّمَةٍ` and `كِرَامٍ` at 80:13 and 80:16 repeat status language. The packet supplies both spatial and social elevation; no disambiguation is necessary. The sheets read as placed above contamination and ranked above the prestige calculus corrected earlier.

2. **Elevation is paired with mediated nearness.** `ر ف ع B004` supplies bringing near or presenting, and 80:15 immediately locates the sheets in hands. I infer that the carriers bridge the distance implied by raised status. This reverses a simple remote-height reading: `مَّرْفُوعَةٍ` marks authority that is presented through mediation, not authority withheld by distance.

3. **Purity becomes a capacity to purify conduct.** `ط ه ر B001` supplies purity with defilement removed; `ط ه ر B004` supplies a pure medium able to purify another, and `ط ه ر B005` supplies cleansing conduct from blame. The purified sheets stand between the fearful recipient at 80:9-12 and the ungrateful human at 80:17-19. The packet does not state that the medium causes moral cleansing; I infer this from reminder reception plus the pure carrier. `مُّطَهَّرَةٍ` therefore describes both protected content and latent corrective function.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:15-16 resolved the apparent distance of elevation by putting the sheets in skilled, trustworthy hands. 80:17-19 then made the purifying-medium reading consequential: protected content confronts blameworthy conduct rather than remaining ceremonially clean.

findings.text: Yükseltilme ve arındırılma, sayfaların değerini seçkin muhatapların ilgisinden bağımsız, korunmuş ve nesnel bir konuma yerleştirir.
Hemen ardından sayfaların ellere verilmesi, yüksek konumu erişilmez uzaklık değil, güvenilir aracılarla yakına getirilen yetki olarak gösterir.
Arınmış sayfalar, yalnız kirden korunmuş bir nesne değil, alan kişinin davranışını da temizleyebilecek bir araç olarak okunabilir.
Sonraki su ve ürün dizisi üzerinden, sayfaların arınması ve yükseltilmesi temizleyici suyla yetişip kaldırılan ürüne benzetilebilir.

morphemes_tsv.note: ayah attribution taken from morpheme_id/word_id, never from the qac_ref column: basmalah rows are a000 but carry surah 1's qac_refs

word_morpheme_spans.note: word_analysis critical words are orthographic/analytic units, not QAC words; each resolves to a MORPHEME SPAN. The upstream aligned_qac_word_ref is preserved verbatim in word_analysis and is NOT corrected here -- renumbering would fabricate identities (PRINCIPLES.md §11 / basmalah no-hidden-renumbering rule). Use word_morpheme_spans for any word-level join to QAC.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref resolves against qac_morphemes for this ayah

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_focus_trace_hermetic.note: Hermetic Focus Trace not requested for this bundle. Rebuild with --include-focus-trace, or --require-focus-trace when reader JSON must be present.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
